result:
Round 298 is done: I copied B's three sketch files into the repo exactly as written, and every check I ran passed. Two things need B's decision: one setup file was missing before I started, and the code-reviewer found a Medium gap, so the hydration-warning check (GATE297-F1) is only partly fixed.

**Changed files** (only the three this round allows; each matches its sketch byte for byte; no app, frozen or protected file touched):
- `app/lib/arrangement/__tests__/studio-link-hydrate-ssr-ui.test.tsx` (new; LH3 now lives here on its own)
- `app/lib/arrangement/__tests__/studio-link-hydrate-ui.test.tsx`
- `docs/implementation/2026/quarter-IV/220-studio-link-deep-link.md`

**Claims script:** the run before editing matched the expected output except K11: `b-round-297/sketch.patch` is missing. The loop's `.gitignore` drops `loop/**/*.patch` (confirmed with `git check-ignore`), so the file didn't carry over to this machine. The three sketch files I actually copy were all present. I rebuilt the patch as `a-round-298/reconstructed-sketch.patch` and it matches what the task describes. I treated this as an environment gap and went ahead rather than stopping; B decides whether that was right. If B calls it a STOP, these three copies are the only changes in the repo. After editing, only the allowed differences appeared, plus the same K11 gap.

**Checks I ran:**
- `npm run typecheck` and `npm run lint`: both rc 0. Lint shows 205 warnings and 1 info across the repo, none in the owned files.
- Biome on the two test files: no findings.
- Covering set: 7 files, 58 tests, all pass. LH3 now runs from the new file in 560 ms. The slowest test is NG5 at 2,270 ms of its 15 s timeout, and nothing is above 50 % of its timeout.
- LH3's error output contains only the server-side `useLayoutEffect` warnings and the known `muted` mismatch.
- The full suite and the build are left to the root gate.

**Mutants** (on a separate copy with its own Vite cache; every file restored and confirmed identical afterwards). All match B's expectations:

| Mutant | Result |
|---|---|
| (h) attribute that differs between server and client | LH3 fails |
| (e) remove the preview selection prop | LH1 and LH3 fail |
| (g) remove the focus-settled line | LH4 fails |
| (i) start the error spy before the server render | LH3 passes (expected) |
| Vacuity: drop the library reorder | LH3 fails |
| Control: (h) against the old HEAD test file | all 4 pass, which reproduces the original bug |

**Code review** (score 7/10, no Critical). I fixed none of the findings, because the task requires the files to match the sketches exactly. They go to B as A-R298-REVIEW-1 to -7:
- **REVIEW-1 (Medium, confirmed in react-dom 18.3.1):** the new, narrower warning filter misses two other React warnings that use up the same one-warning-per-load allowance: "Extra attributes from the server" and "Did not expect server HTML…". So LH3 now catches a changed attribute value, but not an attribute or node that only the server adds. GATE297-F1 should not be closed on C PASS alone; it needs a widened filter and a mutant that adds an attribute.
- **REVIEW-2 (Medium, not verified by me):** text or structure mismatches may be reported through React's `onRecoverableError` and never reach `console.error`, so the check would miss them.
- **REVIEW-3 (Medium):** LH3 only works because the library hydrates before the video dock in `StudioWorkspace.tsx`, and no test guards that order.
- **REVIEW-4 (Low):** if hydration throws, that root is never added to the cleanup list. This touches C's cleanup row.
- **REVIEW-5 and -6 (Low):** an assertion that cannot currently fail, and the one-hydration-per-file rule being only a convention.
- **REVIEW-7 (Info):** doc 220 still says "9 files, 89 tests", and one sentence says only the warning check moved when the whole LH3 test moved. Both lines are in B's sketch.
- The reviewer had no shell, so it read the final files rather than `git diff`; the root gate review should diff independently.
- **Architecture note** (proposal only, not done): move the duplicated setup and helpers shared by the two test files into one shared test helper.

I did not run a browser, since no app code changed. C's browser rows (B-COLD-DEEPLINK, G298-AUTH), the doc row and C's own mutant runs are still open.

The report is `tmp/studio-real-loop/a-round-298.md`, with the logs in `tmp/studio-real-loop/a-round-298/`.
